title: Do active polar thin-film drops dewetted from a noisy film run and split into persistent daughters on a 2D substrate, where a plain-diffusion twin makes no drops at all?
summary: Trinschek, Stegemerten, John & Thiele (PRE 101, 062802, 2020, arXiv:1911.08258) couple a lubrication thin film with a wetting potential to a polarization field. On 1D substrates, uniformly polarized ridges move at any alpha0 != 0 (Fig. 14 uses alpha0 = 0.002). At c_a = -0.05 with alpha0 = 0, a two-domain ridge splits into two resting, oppositely polarized daughters (Figs 16-17). Splitting on 2D substrates has since been published. Stegemerten, John & Thiele, Soft Matter 18, 5823 (2022), DOI 10.1039/D2SM00648K (https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.08961), simulate 3D drops on an 800x800 substrate with no self-propulsion. At strong polarization-surface coupling c_hpa and large active stress, 'large drops split into smaller ones', and splitting continues until surface tension dominates, giving 'ensembles of smaller steadily moving drops' (Fig. 1(a)-(c); smaller-volume phase diagram in Fig. 6). No published work found here covers four things: many drops dewetted from a noisy film, self-propulsion combined with splitting, merge/split (fission-fusion) statistics, or regrowth of daughters by condensation. The question should be framed around those. Experiment fixes: (1) Add a 2D positive control that reproduces the yellow splitting region of the 2022 Fig. 1(a) from a single large drop. (2) Include the PS coupling term (c_hpa, the coupling of polarization to the free-surface gradient), because the 2020 ridge reduction drops it and the 2022 paper needs strong c_hpa for 2D splitting. Without it, the main sweep may not split at all. (3) Note that the 2020 1D splitting at c_a = -0.05 was run at alpha0 = 0, so the 1D control should split at alpha0 = 0 and move at alpha0 = 0.002 as separate checks.
experiment:
Positive control (about 25 min). A y-invariant ridge (effectively 1D) at the published parameters (A = M = h_a = eta = gamma = 1, c_sp = 0.01, c_p = 2, Q_NC = 1).
- Expected: a uniformly polarized ridge moves at alpha0 = 0.002, and a two-domain drop splits at c_a = -0.05 (Figs 16-17).
- Numerics: the new-dynamics sweep's stabilized semi-implicit spectral step (max(h^3/3) gamma k^4 implicit, the rest explicit) at dt = 0.25.
- Its passive check at 128^2 (h0 = 2 + 0.05 noise) dewetted into 11-12 drops on a precursor film, with mass conserved to 1e-4, at 4.6 ms per step. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-physim/a7c2ec48-e3a6-5436-88da-a7523dbbe428/scratchpad/tf/tf2.py.
- Use h0 ~ 2: at h0 = 10 the fastest dewetting wavelength is ~500 dx.

Main (about 45 min). A 2D noisy film with noisy height-integrated polarization P on 160^2.
- c_a in {0, -0.05} x alpha0 in {0.005, 0.02}, 2 seeds, 2-4e4 steps.
- labkit counts drops, splits, merges, persistent daughters and body lengths travelled.
- Report the merge/split ratio: colliding drops coalesce, which can give a fission-fusion foam.

Twin. Replace the lubrication flux with D lap h at a matched rate, keeping the active terms. Expect no bounded drops.

If time remains. Add the gradient-dynamics condensation term -Q_ev(dF/dh - mu_v), with mu_v just above drop coexistence, to test whether daughters regrow and split again.
